environment.isolation: remote-free disposable clones; canonical repository read-only except final audit artifacts

findings.title: Strict production gate publishes residual reference and not-authorized copy
findings.preconditions: A disposable template clone is initialized with non-sample identity and canonical domain; publication approvals and approved privacy text are supplied.
findings.root_cause: Reference-state copy is hard-coded and rendered unconditionally in pages/components, while check-public-output.ts owns only a narrow literal sentinel list. The project-mode production gate has no general rule preventing reference/not-authorized/pending-verification UI.
reproduction_steps: Create a remote-free disposable clone and reuse only local locked dependencies.
Run: python docs/audits/adversarial-validation-2026-08-27/harness/lifecycle.py <disposable-clone>.
Verify all fourteen lifecycle steps return exit 0.
Search the disposable dist directory for: Estado de la referencia, Publicación: No autorizada, Referencia; no representa un negocio real, and pending-verification/reference phrases.
findings.expected_behavior: A strict client-production gate rejects output that says publication is unauthorized, the business is not real, or facts remain pending verification.
findings.observed_behavior: All fourteen steps passed. The built Taller Nopal site still contained reference/not-authorized/pending-verification copy in public HTML.
evidence: lifecycle-results.json records fourteen exit-0 steps.
src/components/core/SiteFooter.astro:26 emits 'Referencia; no representa un negocio real.'.
src/components/sections/StatusRegister.astro:3 and :8 emit reference/publication state.
src/components/sections/ServicesGrid.astro:18 emits pending structured-information copy.
src/pages/contacto.astro:23 emits reference-data replacement copy.
src/pages/nosotros.astro:16 emits pending-verification credentials copy.
scripts/check-public-output.ts does not own equivalent generic reference-state sentinels.
findings.reproducibility: 1/1 complete lifecycle; independently confirmed by a separate read-only agent
findings.files_modified_by_experiment: Disposable lifecycle clone only; canonical source unchanged.
findings.prior_finding_relationship: Distinct extension of remediated AV2-001. AV2-001 covered canonical data-domain placeholders; this finding covers unconditional presentation copy that remains after those remediations.
findings.proposed_remediation: Replace unconditional reference copy with state-derived production-safe content, and make project-mode output scanning reject a centrally owned set of reference/not-authorized/pending-verification states. The gate should derive allowed publication state from canonical data rather than free-text coincidence alone.
findings.proposed_regression_test: Build an approved project fixture, concatenate visible dist HTML text, and assert every owned reference-state sentinel is absent. The test must fail against this commit and pass only when production rendering or validation is corrected.
findings.suggested_next_experiment: After remediation, rerun the full fourteen-step lifecycle and assert both gate success and absence of every centrally enumerated reference-state marker.

findings.title: Initializer filesystem failure leaves a mixed canonical state
findings.preconditions: Template mode; valid client input; the final canonical target memory.toml becomes unwritable after planning but before its write.
findings.root_cause: scripts/init-client.ts performs sequential direct writeFileSync calls without temporary files, atomic commit, rollback, lock, or post-write verification.
reproduction_steps: Create a disposable clone and record hashes of src/config/site.ts, src/data/business.json, and memory.toml.
Make only memory.toml read-only.
Run the client initializer with valid client input.
Restore permissions and compare the three files with their original hashes.
findings.expected_behavior: A failed initialization leaves all canonical owners byte-identical, or leaves an explicitly recoverable transaction marker.
findings.observed_behavior: The command exited 1 with EPERM on the final write. site.ts and business.json contained Taller Nopal/client data and a new site identity; memory.toml remained in template mode.
evidence: Disposable git diff contained src/config/site.ts and src/data/business.json only.
memory.toml remained mode=template.
scripts/init-client.ts:355 is the uncovered sequential write loop.
Coverage inspection showed the successful filesystem write block was not exercised by tests.
findings.reproducibility: 1/1 injected final-write permission fault; independently confirmed by a separate read-only agent
findings.files_modified_by_experiment: Disposable partial-write clone only; permissions restored before cleanup.
findings.proposed_remediation: Write all candidates to same-directory temporary files, fsync where appropriate, then commit with an atomic/rollback protocol. Serialize initialization with a lock or atomic claim and report recovery steps if rollback itself fails.
findings.proposed_regression_test: Inject failure into the third write and assert nonzero exit plus byte-identical hashes for all three canonical targets.
findings.suggested_next_experiment: Fault each write and rename boundary independently, including rollback failure, in a disposable fixture.

findings.title: Public URL fields accept and emit unsafe schemes while production validation passes
findings.preconditions: An operator or future ingestion path writes a syntactically valid non-web URL into a canonical public-link field; tested with locations[0].mapUrl='javascript:alert(1)'.
findings.root_cause: Generic z.url() syntax validation is treated as an HTTP(S) allowlist. check-links.ts deliberately skips references beginning with a scheme, and production/output validation has no disallowed-scheme rule.
reproduction_steps: Prepare an otherwise passing initialized lifecycle clone.
Set src/data/locations.json mapUrl to javascript:alert(1).
Run npm run validate:data, npm run build, and npm run quality:production.
Search dist/index.html and dist/contacto/index.html for javascript:alert(1).
findings.expected_behavior: Fields rendered as web navigation or asset URLs reject non-HTTP(S) schemes before build, or the built-output gate rejects them.
findings.observed_behavior: Data validation, build, and the full production gate passed; both built routes contained href='javascript:alert(1)'.
evidence: src/schemas/common.ts:12 defines NullableUrlSchema as z.url().nullable().
src/schemas/location.ts:51 applies it to mapUrl.
src/components/sections/Locations.astro:31 emits mapUrl directly as href.
A pure schema probe also accepted data:, mailto:, and tel: URL forms.
The current built CSP has script-src 'self' plus hashes and no unsafe-inline; this should block execution of the tested javascript URL in conforming browsers.
findings.reproducibility: 1/1 artifact mutation; schema behavior independently confirmed
findings.security_scope_note: Confirmed broken-link/unsafe-sink behavior; executable XSS was not demonstrated and is materially mitigated by the present CSP. CSP retention and future trust changes remain dependencies.
findings.proposed_remediation: Introduce semantic field-specific schemas that allow only http: and https:, with HTTPS required where appropriate. Add a final artifact scan rejecting dangerous href/src schemes regardless of source schema.
findings.proposed_regression_test: Schema tests reject javascript:, data:, file:, vbscript:, userinfo, and inappropriate mailto:/tel: values; a built-output fixture containing a disallowed href must fail the production gate.
findings.suggested_next_experiment: After schema hardening, fuzz URL normalization, Unicode hostnames, credentials, ports, redirects, and encoded schemes without activating links.

findings.title: Tests do not protect production-gate script composition
findings.preconditions: The package.json quality:production script is accidentally or maliciously replaced while individual validator implementations remain unchanged.
findings.root_cause: Tests invoke individual validators and ordinary npm test suites, but no test asserts the owner script's required ordered composition or exercises it against a production-ready fixture.
reproduction_steps: In a disposable clone, replace package.json quality:production with node -e "process.exit(0)".
Run npm test.
Run npm run quality:production.
findings.expected_behavior: A mutation that removes every strict production step is detected by a contract or integration test.
findings.observed_behavior: npm test passed in full, and the mutated production command returned 0 without running any validator or build.
evidence: Current package.json:28 contains the correct fourteen-step chain.
The disposable no-op mutant passed npm test.
CI invokes quality:production in project mode, but would invoke the same no-op owner if this mutation landed.
findings.prior_finding_relationship: Narrower than AV-009 and distinct from remediated C4-002: the automated path now exists, but its package-script composition is not itself protected.
findings.proposed_remediation: Add a package-script contract that parses the script into the exact owned ordered steps, and run the real owner command against a minimal initialized fixture in CI.
findings.proposed_regression_test: The no-op mutation and deletion/reordering of any required step must make the test fail.
findings.suggested_next_experiment: Use bounded mutation testing to remove one gate step at a time and verify every mutant is killed.

findings.title: Link validator accepts a directory that has no index artifact
findings.preconditions: A built asset references an internal extensionless path whose filesystem target exists only as a directory with no index.html.
findings.root_cause: scripts/check-links.ts accepts existsSync(base) without requiring a file or resolving a directory to index.html.
reproduction_steps: In a disposable built dist, create directory-target/placeholder.txt but no directory-target/index.html.
Create dist/probe.css containing a reference to /directory-target.
Run node scripts/check-links.ts.
findings.expected_behavior: An internal route is valid only if it resolves to a deployable file, or a directory containing index.html under the documented hosting contract.
findings.observed_behavior: The validator printed PASSED because the directory itself existed.
evidence: scripts/check-links.ts:57 selects base when existsSync(base) is true.
The synthetic directory-without-index fixture passed.
findings.proposed_remediation: Use statSync to distinguish files from directories; for a directory require index.html (or an explicitly documented provider rule).
findings.proposed_regression_test: Directory without index fails; directory with index passes; regular file and extension fallback cases retain expected behavior.
findings.suggested_next_experiment: Add Windows/Linux separator and encoded-path cases after the minimal fix.

findings.title: WebKit form assertion reports a missing payload although the POST body is correct
findings.preconditions: Run the tablet-webkit Playwright form smoke test on the recorded Windows host.
findings.root_cause: tests/browser/smoke.spec.ts asserts route.request().postData() text, which was empty in failing WebKit interceptions even though retained request bytes and decoded parameters were complete.
reproduction_steps: Run the tablet-webkit contact-form test three times with one worker and trace retention.
Inspect the failing request trace body bytes and parsed form parameters.
findings.expected_behavior: The test evaluates the submitted request body through a representation reliable for the browser engine.
findings.observed_behavior: The assertion failed 2/3 times. Both failed traces recorded bodySize=127, correct URL-encoded fields, and successful navigation to the thank-you page; the third run passed.
evidence: tests/browser/smoke.spec.ts:66 reads postData().
Failed traces contained the expected form-name, bot-field, nombre, correo, and mensaje bytes.
The product-level hypothesis 'form sends no payload' was falsified.
findings.reproducibility: 2 failures and 1 pass across 3 repeated runs
findings.files_modified_by_experiment: Trace/test-result artifacts in disposable/test output only.
findings.proposed_remediation: Assert postDataBuffer or decoded server/interception parameters instead of relying only on postData text.
findings.proposed_regression_test: A WebKit test submits Unicode and spaces, then compares decoded field values from the request buffer.
findings.suggested_next_experiment: Verify the corrected oracle on current Ubuntu WebKit and Windows WebKit.

findings.title: Windows WebKit documentation is stale and the iPad skip-link oracle is non-portable
findings.preconditions: Run the configured tablet-webkit project on the current Windows host.
findings.root_cause: Browser-support documents preserve an obsolete psl-5.dll launch limitation. The skip-link test assumes synthetic Tab focus behavior in an iPad/touch WebKit emulation without recording activeElement or separating programmatic activation from hardware-keyboard traversal.
reproduction_steps: Launch the tablet-webkit project on Windows.
Repeat the skip-link smoke test three times with one worker.
Compare the launch evidence with docs/spec/accessibility.md and docs/spec/browser-support.md.
findings.expected_behavior: Documentation describes current capability and tests distinguish focus-navigation environment limitations from product target-focus behavior.
findings.observed_behavior: WebKit launched successfully, contradicting the documented DLL block. The skip test failed 3/3 at the first synthetic Tab focus assertion and never executed Enter or the target-focus assertion.
evidence: docs/spec/accessibility.md:15 and docs/spec/browser-support.md:13 say WebKit cannot run on the current Windows host.
Retained traces identify browserName=webkit and platform=win32.
The skip-link anchor precedes the header and the target owns tabindex=-1; no active-element trace established a markup defect.
findings.reproducibility: WebKit launch 1/1; skip Tab failure 3/3; product focus defect not established
findings.proposed_remediation: Update docs to say Windows WebKit launches but the current project is not green. Split skip-link tests into programmatic focus/activation and environment-specific sequential-keyboard coverage; capture activeElement diagnostics.
findings.proposed_regression_test: Programmatically focus the skip link, activate it, and assert main focus; run sequential Tab separately only on environments where hardware keyboard semantics are supported.
findings.suggested_next_experiment: Run current HEAD on GitHub-hosted Ubuntu WebKit and real Safari/iPad hardware before assigning product severity.

findings.title: Repository-wide secret scan is explicitly not configured
findings.preconditions: Run the configured memory check suite or inspect memory.toml.
findings.root_cause: memory.toml sets checks.secret_scan to an empty array, which the validation contract intentionally reports as NOT_CONFIGURED rather than a failure.
reproduction_steps: Run python ops/memory_health.py --json.
Inspect the secret_scan result and memory.toml [checks].
findings.expected_behavior: A repository that declares a no-secrets invariant has an automated high-confidence secret-scanning control, or clearly treats its absence as an unresolved release risk.
findings.observed_behavior: The overall configured check run passed while secret_scan was NOT_CONFIGURED.
evidence: memory.toml:8 is secret_scan = [].
docs/spec/validation.md defines an empty array as NOT_CONFIGURED.
gitleaks, TruffleHog, Semgrep, Trivy, and Syft were unavailable on the host.
Campaign regex scans of current tree and full Git history found no high-confidence credential signatures; this reduces immediate concern but does not close the control gap.
findings.proposed_remediation: Configure a pinned, reviewed secret scanner in CI and memory.toml, with redaction-safe output and explicit baseline/allowlist ownership.
findings.proposed_regression_test: A synthetic fixture containing a fake provider token is rejected; ordinary sample/public values pass; logs redact the token body.
findings.suggested_next_experiment: Evaluate a deterministic scanner in a disposable branch without sending repository content to external services.

findings.title: Concurrent initializer race duplicates accepted finding AV2-006
findings.preconditions: Two valid initializers begin against the same template-mode working tree.
findings.root_cause: Time-of-check to time-of-use gap around mode validation and unsynchronized sequential writes.
reproduction_steps: Barrier-launch two initializer processes with different valid client fixtures in one disposable clone.
Record both exit codes and the final three canonical owners.
Repeat ten times, restoring template state between trials.
findings.expected_behavior: Exactly one caller succeeds; the other receives ALREADY_INITIALIZED.
findings.observed_behavior: Both callers returned 0 in 10/10 trials. Final state was internally consistent but scheduler-dependent: client A won once and client B nine times; mixed state was not observed.
evidence: Twenty successful process exits across ten trials.
Final winner distribution A=1, B=9, mixed=0.
AV2-006 already records the same root cause and is deliberately accepted for the documented single-operator workflow.
findings.files_modified_by_experiment: Disposable concurrency fixture only; restored after each trial.
findings.proposed_remediation: Address together with C5-002 using an atomic claim/lock and transactional write protocol if concurrent automation becomes supported.
findings.proposed_regression_test: Barrier-synchronized subprocess test asserting one success, one ALREADY_INITIALIZED, and one internally consistent winner.
findings.suggested_next_experiment: None within the current accepted-risk workflow; do not inflate this duplicate as a new finding.
